strengths: The paper targets an important practical bottleneck in equivariant atomistic models: edge-wise tensor materialization and costly SO(3) contractions. A genuinely fused sparse-attention implementation could have substantial utility for large molecular systems.

The combination of axis-aligned SO(2) sparsification with node-centric factorization is conceptually interesting. The manuscript also provides an intuitive systems motivation, an online-softmax algorithm, and low-degree examples of the proposed re-indexing.

The reported efficiency results are potentially significant: EAAS is reported to accelerate tensor products by roughly 6×, while the custom attention implementation substantially reduces memory and allows inference on systems containing up to 100,000 atoms.

Evaluation covers two large molecular datasets, direct and conservative force models, several efficiency baselines, and an initial molecular-dynamics application. The manuscript is generally readable and its figures and tables are visually clear.
No material research-ethics concern is apparent from the described experiments, which use established molecular datasets and synthetic benchmark structures.
weaknesses: The central exactness claim is not established as written. Equation (2) defines solid spherical harmonics with radial dependence ||r||^ell, but Proposition 4.3 and its proof drop the proportionality factor after pole alignment: the right-hand side of Equation (14), as defined by Equation (13), depends on the direction through D_R but not on ||r||. It therefore cannot equal h tensor-product R^(ell_f)(r) for general radii and ell_f>0 unless an omitted radial factor is restored.

The architectural equations do not clearly implement the E2Former factorization they cite. Equation (5) contains a sum over u, binomial coefficients, signs, and Wigner-6j recoupling paths, whereas Equations (8)–(10) replace this with two generic tensor products without specifying how those terms and path weights are represented. Consequently, translation invariance/equivariance is particularly unclear because the implementation uses spherical harmonics of absolute positions r_i and r_j.

The claimed fused, on-the-fly attention is contradicted by Appendix A. Algorithm 1 performs online softmax without storing edge scores, but the provided benchmark implementation explicitly creates `scores` and `alpha` tensors of shape N×K×H using separate QK, softmax, and value kernels. Thus the implementation used for Figure 1 does materialize edge-level attention tensors, contrary to the headline claim that attention weights and edge intermediates are eliminated.

The asymptotic memory discussion is imprecise. The method still stores an N×K neighbor-index tensor and processes every interaction, while the paper assumes bounded K so that both O(|E|)=O(KN) and O(|V|) are linear in N. The demonstrated benefit is primarily a potentially valuable constant-factor reduction in activation memory, not an elimination of edge complexity as repeatedly stated.

Only the forward kernel is described. No backward algorithm, backward-memory analysis, gradient-correctness test, or training-throughput result is supplied, despite claims that large models can be trained efficiently and that training throughput is improved. This is especially important for conservative-force training, which involves differentiation through predicted energies.

The efficiency evidence is insufficiently controlled. The 20× kernel result is only against a naive PyTorch implementation; operation counting for the reported TFLOPS is unspecified, no comparison to optimized sparse-attention libraries is given, and no numerical-error or equivariance tests validate the custom Triton implementation. End-to-end comparisons omit model parameter counts, representation sizes, precision, compilation settings, and matched accuracy/compute controls.

The predictive evaluation is not reproducible from the manuscript. It omits dataset splits, preprocessing, training schedules, loss weights, cutoff and neighbor construction, architectural hyperparameters, parameter counts, seeds, error bars, and the provenance or retraining protocol for many baseline values. The stated code link is empty. These omissions also make the accuracy and throughput comparisons difficult to interpret fairly.

Some empirical conclusions overstate the tables. E2Former-V2 is competitive rather than uniformly superior on SPICE and OMol25, and the single water RDF plot lacks simulation settings, uncertainty, stability diagnostics, and broader observables; it does not by itself establish accurate long-term dynamics or superior many-body modeling.

Presentation requires technical tightening: Equation (6) has unclear concatenation/transposition dimensions, the direct equivariant force head is not defined, the exact relationship between EAAS and Wigner-6j recoupling remains underspecified, and there is no dedicated limitations discussion. The lack of a limitations section is not itself disqualifying, but the manuscript fails to acknowledge hardware dependence, fixed-degree assumptions, missing backward evaluation, and the restricted MD validation.

strengths: The paper targets an important practical bottleneck: edge-wise activation materialization in equivariant molecular models. Avoiding gathered key/value tensors could substantially improve scalability even when the underlying arithmetic remains edge-linear.

The combination of axis-aligned SO(2) sparsification with hardware-aware Triton kernels is potentially useful. The reported forward benchmarks—approximately 6× for tensor products and 20× for attention—are promising, and the 100k-atom results suggest practical engineering value if independently reproduced.

The high-level exposition is generally accessible. Figures 2–4, the online-softmax pseudocode, and the separation between algebraic and systems components make the intended computation understandable.
The evaluation includes predictive accuracy, kernel efficiency, end-to-end throughput, memory, and a molecular-dynamics example rather than reporting speed alone.
weaknesses: Soundness: Proposition 4.3 appears mathematically incomplete. Since Eq. (2) defines solid spherical harmonics with a ||r||^ℓ factor, the pole value in Eq. (27) is only proportional to δm,0 and retains radius-dependent magnitude. Yet the re-indexing operator in Eqs. (13)/(25) contains no such factor. Consequently, the claimed exact equality in Eq. (14) cannot hold as written; for example, with ℓi=0 and ℓf=ℓo=1, its left side scales with ||r|| while its right side does not.

Soundness: The transition from the cited E2Former factorization in Eq. (5) to the implemented pipeline in Eqs. (8)–(10) is not established. Eq. (5) contains a sum over u, degree-dependent source/target harmonics, signs, and Wigner-6j recoupling weights, whereas these components disappear from the proposed three-stage formulation. The manuscript therefore does not prove that the actual architecture preserves the claimed exact factorization, translation behavior, or equivariance.

Soundness/evidence: Appendix A contradicts the central fused-attention claim. Algorithm 1 describes a single streaming online-softmax reduction that never stores edge scores, but the provided benchmark implementation explicitly creates scores and alpha tensors of shape N×K×H and invokes separate QK, softmax, and value kernels. Thus the evaluated code sketch still materializes edge-level attention and is not the algorithm used to justify the claimed memory complexity.

The asymptotic framing is misleading. The method still stores an N×K neighbor-index tensor and performs a key/value access for every interaction. With bounded K, both O(|E|)=O(KN) and O(|V|)=O(N) are already linear in N; the demonstrated benefit is potentially an important constant-factor and activation-width reduction, not elimination of edge computation.

The empirical narrative contains a direct numerical error: the text states that conservative E2Former-V2 has total OMol25 energy MAE 1.27, but Table 2 reports 2.09; 1.27 belongs to eSEN-sm-cons. The tables also show mixed rather than uniformly superior accuracy—for example, E2Former-V2 does not achieve the best aggregate SPICE force error. These results do not support repeated claims of broadly “superior performance.”

The efficiency comparisons are insufficiently controlled. Model parameter counts, widths, precisions, compilation settings, and matched accuracy/capacity are not reported. Figure 1 compares against dense PyTorch SDPA with a pre-built attention mask, which is not a convincing sparse-FlashAttention baseline, while the “Traditional EGNN” baseline is a simple materializing implementation. Table 3 compares heterogeneous architectures and force modes on synthetic FCC-carbon inputs with PBC disabled, without uncertainty estimates.

Claims about efficient training are unsupported: the kernel and tensor-product experiments measure only forward passes, and no backward-kernel latency, gradient-memory usage, training throughput, or numerical-gradient validation is provided. Numerical tests of equivariance and equality to the dense tensor product are also absent.

Reproducibility is inadequate. The advertised code link is blank, and the paper omits essential training configurations, architecture sizes, dataset splits/subsampling, optimizer schedules, cutoffs for the accuracy experiments, seeds, repeated-run statistics, and baseline reproduction procedures. Configuration fragments for one throughput benchmark are not enough to reproduce the main results.

The molecular-dynamics evidence is only one RDF plot. Simulation duration, time step, ensemble, temperature, equilibration, stability statistics, uncertainty, and the experimental reference are missing, so the claim about accurate long-term dynamics and hydrogen-bond networks is not supported.

Originality and significance are limited by the current evidence: axis alignment follows eSCN, node-centric recoupling follows E2Former, and online-softmax kernel fusion follows FlashAttention. Their combination may be a valuable systems contribution, but the paper does not isolate which component is novel or demonstrate that its purported exact algebra and fully fused implementation are realized.

Limitations are not treated appropriately. There is no substantive discussion of dependence on Triton/H20 hardware, fixed neighbor budgets, irregular neighbor distributions, preprocessing and neighbor-list costs, higher angular orders, backward-pass support, or portability. No major human-subject or societal ethical concern is apparent, but compute/resource usage and dataset/licensing considerations are also unaddressed. Overall, the central mathematical and implementation claims require correction and substantially stronger verification before others could reliably build on the work.

strengths: The paper addresses an important practical problem: edge-feature materialization substantially limits the scale of high-order equivariant molecular models. Combining node-centric factorization, SO(2)-aligned sparse tensor products, and hardware-aware attention is a useful and potentially significant direction.

The EAAS formulation is presented with explicit propositions, parity rules, low-degree examples, and an appendix derivation. This gives the mathematical component more substance than a purely implementation-driven optimization paper.

The reported efficiency results are promising: approximately 6× faster tensor products, roughly 20× kernel throughput improvements, substantially lower peak memory, and execution at up to 100,000 atoms on one H20 GPU. The scaling trends are consistent with the intended reduction in HBM traffic.

Predictive results are broadly competitive on SPICE and OMol25, indicating that the efficiency-oriented design does not obviously destroy model quality. The bulk-water RDF experiment also provides an initial application-level check beyond static errors.

The paper is generally organized around a clear motivation-to-method-to-evaluation narrative, and I found no material research-ethics concerns in the described datasets or experiments. weaknesses: The central implementation claim is contradicted by Appendix A. Algorithm 1 describes a fused online-softmax reduction that never materializes edge scores, but the provided reference snippet first constructs scores and alpha tensors of shape N×K×H before calling a separate value kernel. This is not the claimed on-the-fly algorithm and leaves unclear which implementation produced Figures 1 and 4.

The asymptotic claim needs qualification. The method still stores an N×K neighbor index and performs O(NK) interactions. With fixed K this is O(N), but the paper itself notes that conventional bounded-degree message passing is also O(KN)=O(N). The demonstrated contribution is primarily removal of large edge-feature activations and associated memory traffic, not elimination of edge complexity in general.

Several empirical claims do not match the tables. The text says the conservative E2Former-V2 obtains total OMol25 energy MAE 1.27, whereas Table 2 reports 2.09; 1.27 belongs to eSEN-sm-cons. Its total force MAE, 8.38, is also slightly worse than eSEN-sm-cons at 8.25. Likewise, the claim of superior SPICE performance overlooks eSEN-Cons.'s substantially better aggregate 0.23/6.36 energy/force errors, albeit with incomplete subset reporting.

The efficiency comparisons are insufficiently controlled. Model parameter counts, precision, batch size, channel dimensions, compilation settings, and matched neighbor policies are not consistently reported. Table 3 compares heterogeneous architectures and direct versus conservative force modes, while Figure 4 only compares the kernel with a naive PyTorch implementation on one H20 GPU. No backward-pass or actual training-throughput results support the claims about efficient training.

Reproducibility is currently inadequate: the abstract's code-availability sentence has no URL; full architecture and training hyperparameters, data splits, checkpoint-selection procedures, random seeds, and variance across runs are absent. There are also no numerical equivariance tests, dense-reference comparisons, or gradient checks for the custom EAAS and Triton implementations.

The evaluation does not isolate the end-to-end effects of EAAS, node-centric factorization, and kernel fusion. Component microbenchmarks are useful, but an ablation reporting accuracy, latency, and memory for matched full-model variants is needed to substantiate the causal claims.

The molecular-dynamics evidence is too limited to support claims about long-term dynamics and hydrogen-bond networks. Only one RDF curve is shown, without simulation duration, timestep, ensemble, temperature, equilibration protocol, independent trajectories, or uncertainty estimates.

Originality is meaningful mainly at the level of synthesis and implementation: SO(2) axis alignment is closely related to eSCN, node-centric Wigner-6j factorization comes from E2Former, and streaming softmax follows FlashAttention. The paper should distinguish the genuinely new algebraic or kernel contribution more precisely.

The manuscript contains no substantive limitations discussion despite important restrictions involving fixed neighbor budgets, absolute-coordinate factorization, Triton/H20 portability, numerical precision, and benchmark representativeness. Given the promising idea but unresolved evidential and reproducibility issues, substantial revision is required before others can reliably build on the contribution.

strengths: The paper targets an important systems bottleneck in equivariant molecular models. Reducing edge-activation memory could materially enable larger atomistic simulations.

Combining node-centric factorization, axis-aligned SO(2) contractions, and a streamed sparse-attention kernel is a promising hardware-aware design. The online-softmax formulation is conceptually appropriate for avoiding stored attention matrices.
The evaluation is broad in intent, covering SPICE, OMol25, OC20, kernel microbenchmarks, end-to-end ablations, neighbor-density sensitivity, scaling to 100k atoms, and molecular dynamics.
The manuscript is generally well organized, includes useful implementation and complexity appendices, and acknowledges the expressivity trade-off from removing edge-value nonlinearities.
The impact statement appropriately notes molecular-design benefits and general dual-use risks; no unresolved participant-data or privacy concerns are apparent.
weaknesses: Soundness of the central mathematical claim is not established. Proposition 4.3 is called an exact tensor-product identity, but the displayed operator omits the magnitude/normalization of the surviving spherical-harmonic component. The appendices derive an ordinary Clebsch–Gordan reduction rather than the claimed Wigner-6j recoupling, and the parity-dependent real-basis factor is asserted without a complete change-of-basis calculation. The rotation convention is also inconsistent: R is said to map the z-axis to r, while the proof requires Rr to lie on z.

The attention equations are internally inconsistent. Equation 7 defines a scalar invariant score from invariant queries and keys, whereas Appendix D inserts the apparently equivariant feature Fea_ij into the attention coefficient without explaining a scalar contraction. Consequently, rotational invariance of the implemented attention—and equivalence between the analyzed and evaluated model—is unclear.

The implementation description contradicts the main linear-activation claim. Algorithm 1 describes a single streaming online-softmax reduction that never stores edge scores, but Appendix A's code for 'Ours' explicitly creates an N×K×H score tensor, applies a separate softmax, and passes the resulting attention tensor to a second kernel. This materially undermines the claims of a fully fused kernel and elimination of edge-level attention activations.

The efficiency comparisons do not adequately isolate the proposed contribution. Major baselines are naive PyTorch gathers or dense SDPA with an N×N sparse mask, rather than competitive optimized sparse-attention implementations. Results are limited to one H20 GPU and lack variability. Table 5 compares architectures with different sizes, neighbor limits, and force modes; the submitted model is configured for at most 32 neighbors while benchmark descriptions cite roughly 50. Appendix H also says all runs use torch.no_grad(), which conflicts with computing conservative forces through F=-∇E, and even permits unrelated runtime errors to be reported as OOM.

Accuracy evidence is insufficiently controlled. Dataset splits, preprocessing, baseline training protocols, seed counts, and uncertainty are absent. The proposed SPICE model is initialized through OMol25 pretraining, but comparable pretraining for the baselines is not established. Thus small MAE differences cannot reliably support superiority claims.

The molecular-dynamics evidence is too limited for claims of physical faithfulness. The water experiment omits essential simulation duration, timestep, density, thermostat parameters, uncertainty, and a citation for the experimental curve. The protein result reports only a single 2 ns TM-score trace, without replicas or a baseline, so it does not demonstrate refinement or robust long-timescale stability.

Reproducibility is presently poor: the abstract's code-release sentence ends with a blank URL, and neither the Triton implementation nor the modified GROMACS code is supplied. Several architecture and baseline details needed to reproduce the reported numbers remain unspecified.

Limitations are not treated adequately. The paper should explicitly discuss hardware portability, FP32-only kernel behavior, regimes where sparse graphs favor baselines, the reduced value-path expressivity, dependence on bounded neighbor count, and the numerical and periodic-boundary implications of factorizing relative geometry through absolute-coordinate spherical harmonics. These concerns affect the central claims rather than merely the scope.

strengths: Originality/significance: The paper targets an important practical bottleneck in equivariant atomistic models and combines an axis-aligned tensor-product implementation with sparse, hardware-aware attention. A successful implementation could materially improve large-system molecular modeling.

Soundness: The online-softmax formulation in Eqs. (15)–(18) is conceptually appropriate, and the experiments cover kernel-level timing, component ablations, neighbor-density sensitivity, end-to-end inference, predictive accuracy, and molecular dynamics.

Empirical promise: The reported results suggest substantial memory savings, roughly 3x end-to-end gains from the complete system in Table 4, and scalability to 100k-atom synthetic systems. The paper also compares EAAS with optimized libraries rather than only an unoptimized e3nn baseline.
Presentation: The high-level motivation and architecture are generally understandable, and the appendices provide useful hardware, dataset, and hyperparameter details.
Ethics: The impact statement acknowledges molecular-design dual-use risk, and I see no unresolved ethical issue that independently prevents acceptance.
weaknesses: Soundness—the central exactness claim is not established as written. With the paper's definition of solid spherical harmonics, alignment gives R^(lf)_0(Rr) proportional to ||r||^lf, not one. This factor is absent from the EAAS operator in Eq. (13), the alleged exact identity in Eq. (14), and the expansion in Eq. (33). Consequently, Proposition 4.3 is false as stated unless an omitted radial factor or a different normalized encoding is introduced.

Soundness—the derivation from the E2Former factorization to the implemented architecture is incomplete. Eq. (5) contains a sum over u, binomial factors, degree paths, and Wigner-6j recoupling, whereas Eqs. (8)–(10) replace it with two generic tensor products without specifying those terms. The manuscript therefore does not demonstrate that the implemented update is equivalent to Eq. (5), translation invariant, or theoretically exact. No numerical equivariance/translation-invariance test is provided.

Internal inconsistency undermines the principal memory claim. Section 4.4 and Table 11 describe a fused online-softmax kernel that never materializes attention scores and has O(N) activation memory, but Appendix A's implementation used for Figure 1 explicitly writes scores and alpha tensors of shape N x K x H and invokes separate QK, softmax, and value kernels. It is unclear which implementation generated the main benchmarks. Moreover, O(E)=O(kN) and O(N) are both linear in N for the fixed bounded-neighbor setting; the paper repeatedly presents this mainly constant-factor-in-k improvement as a stronger asymptotic change.

The efficiency evidence does not isolate a fair architectural comparison. The headline approximately 20x result is against a naive PyTorch gather implementation and is expressed as achieved TFLOPS, while the end-to-end ablation shows a smaller approximately 3x gain. Table 5 compares models with unspecified precision, parameter counts, channel sizes, neighbor policies, compilation state, and accuracy/throughput tradeoffs. Ten timed iterations and one GPU are insufficient to characterize variability, and no backward-pass or training-throughput measurements support the claim of improved training throughput.

The accuracy comparisons are inadequately controlled. Parameter counts, training budgets, splits, seeds, uncertainty, and checkpoint-selection procedures are largely missing. The proposed SPICE models are pretrained for 17 epochs on OMol25 before 100 SPICE epochs, but the manuscript does not establish comparable pretraining for the SPICE baselines; attributing the gains to EAAS or the attention design is therefore unsupported. Single-run MAEs without error bars also make small differences difficult to interpret.

The molecular-dynamics evidence is too thin for claims of physical fidelity. The water experiment omits the simulation duration, timestep, thermostat details, density/equilibration protocol, uncertainty, and an identifiable citation for the experimental RDF. The protein result reports one short 2 ns trajectory and only TM-score, with no starting-value analysis, replicate trajectories, baseline curve, energy/stability diagnostics, or force-mode specification. A high and nearly flat TM-score does not show that the model guides the structure toward the native conformation.

Reproducibility is currently poor. The promised code URL is blank, the custom Triton implementation and modified GROMACS code are unavailable, and essential information about data preprocessing, splits, baseline configurations, random seeds, training hardware, and benchmark precision is missing. The supplied pseudocode also conflicts with the stated fused algorithm.

Presentation contains consequential ambiguities rather than merely cosmetic issues: Eq. (7), Algorithm 1, and Eq. (35) do not give a consistent placement/normalization of the cutoff factor; Definition 4.2 simultaneously declares mi=mo while its odd-parity branch requires the opposite order; and Figure 1 labels a random-input sparse-attention microbenchmark as 'Traditional EGNNs.' These issues make the method difficult to audit or reimplement.

Overall, the systems direction is promising, but unsupported exactness, contradictory kernel descriptions, uncontrolled empirical comparisons, and absent code affect the central contribution rather than peripheral details. Substantial correction and re-evaluation are needed before others can reliably build on the work.

strengths: The paper targets an important practical bottleneck in equivariant atomistic models: edge-wise activation materialization. Combining algebraic sparsification with hardware-aware sparse attention is useful and potentially impactful.

EAAS provides a plausible exact axis-aligned reformulation of Clebsch–Gordan products, supported by a derivation, low-degree examples, and comparisons against e3nn, cuEquivariance, and OpenEquivariance. The reported 1.5–6× kernel-level improvements are promising.

The empirical scope is broad: SPICE, OMol25, OC20, kernel and end-to-end ablations, scaling to 100k atoms, neighbor-density analysis, and molecular-dynamics demonstrations. Predictive results are generally competitive, including strong SPICE errors and OMol25 aggregate performance.

The paper is visually polished and mostly well organized. It distinguishes direct from conservative force prediction and openly discusses the expressivity trade-off caused by removing the edge value-path nonlinearity.
The impact statement acknowledges molecular-design dual-use risks. I found no unresolved material ethical concern.
weaknesses: The central implementation and memory claim is internally inconsistent. Algorithm 1 describes a single fused online-softmax reduction that never stores edge scores, but Appendix A's implementation of “Ours” first produces scores and alpha tensors of shape N×K×H using two kernels. This is O(NK) activation storage, contrary to the repeatedly claimed O(N) memory and “no edge-level intermediates.” The manuscript must clarify which implementation produced each result and report measured memory components.

The actual attention rule in Appendix D is materially different from Eqs. 6–7 and raises an equivariance concern. Equation 34 applies an ordinary pointwise nonlinearity to non-scalar irrep components, which is not generally SO(3)-equivariant, and Eq. 35 appears to use the resulting feature in a supposedly scalar attention coefficient without defining the required invariant contraction. No numerical equivariance tests are provided.

The theoretical bridge is incomplete. Equation 5 contains a sum over binomial orders and Wigner-6j recoupling, whereas the three-stage implementation in Eqs. 8–10 suppresses these structures. Meanwhile, the EAAS proof treats an ordinary Clebsch–Gordan product rather than explicitly showing how the claimed Wigner-6j contractions reduce to the implemented operator. Thus the equivalence between the advertised exact factorization and the actual architecture is not established clearly enough.

Efficiency evidence is not yet fully convincing. The headline approximately 20× result compares primarily with a naive PyTorch materializing implementation on one H20 GPU and one precision regime. Table 3 measures forward tensor products only, without backward latency or numerical-error checks. End-to-end baselines lack sufficiently detailed versions and matched settings, and failures from “other runtime errors” are labeled OOM. The paper also claims improved training throughput but reports essentially inference measurements.

Accuracy comparisons lack seeds, uncertainty, split details, controlled parameter or training budgets, and matched retraining of baselines. Consequently, the tables show that the submitted models are competitive but do not isolate whether EAAS and fused attention preserve accuracy under controlled conditions.

The molecular-dynamics evidence is too underspecified for claims of physical fidelity: the protein identity, preparation, timestep, thermostat details, trajectory replicates, uncertainty, reference-RDF citation, and quantitative RDF errors are absent. A stable TM-score over only 2 ns does not by itself demonstrate accurate dynamics or refinement toward the native structure.

Reproducibility is inadequate. The abstract says code is released but the URL is blank; the Triton implementation, backward pass, preprocessing and splits, complete training resources, baseline configurations, and random seeds are unavailable. These omissions are especially consequential because the main contribution is implementation-dependent.

The relationship to prior SO(2) axis-alignment methods such as eSCN and EquiformerV2 is discussed, but the originality of EAAS itself is not sharply separated from those established reductions. Overall, the systems direction is promising, but the central correctness and memory claims need reconciliation before others can reliably build on it.
